title.en: A fort built by a queen

text.en: Aarav and Ananya see a picture of a grand fort in the newspaper, and their Chachi tells them about Maheshwar Fort, built by Queen Ahilya Bai on the banks of the Narmada River. In this chapter you will read the conversation, learn words like majestic and overhanging, find words with similar meanings, spot silent letters, use the articles a, an and the, and read about the famous Maheshwari sarees.

One pleasant evening Aarav and Ananya sat with their Chachi, their paternal aunt, and saw a picture of a grand fort in the newspaper. Chachi told them it was the majestic Maheshwar Fort, built long ago by Queen Ahilya Bai. The fort is famous for its overhanging balconies, which seem to float in the air. Aarav and Ananya were excited to learn that a real queen had built it.
Queen Ahilya Bai ruled Maheshwar in Madhya Pradesh, about 95 kilometres from Indore. She was a warrior queen and belonged to the great Holkar family. She had the fort built on a hill on the banks of the Narmada River, so that she could see her whole kingdom. It is also called Ahilya Fort. She protected her people and built temples, schools and wells. She ruled with kindness and wisdom, and people loved her. A thirteen-feet tall statue of the queen stands in front of the palace even today, like a guardian watching over her land.
The fort is known for its unique style of construction and its grand staircases. It was built with special red stones brought from Gujarat and Rajasthan. It stands on a hill, with the town of Maheshwar on one side and the Narmada River on the other, and many beautifully designed temples are near it. Aarav and Ananya promised to visit one day with Chachi to discover its secrets.
The people of Maheshwar are known for weaving the famous Maheshwari sarees. They were first made of pure silk, but later cotton yarn was introduced, and then a blend of cotton and silk became popular. As they gained popularity, the handloom weaving tradition began in Maheshwar. These sarees are famous for their unique reversible borders and pallus, in colours such as peacock blue, bright yellow, forest green and an Indian red dye called Aal. Today they are sold in India and in other countries.
A fort is a strong building built for defence. Majestic means grand and impressive. Overhanging means sticking out over something below. Balconies are platforms that stick out from the wall of a building. A ruler is a person who governs a country. Unique means one of its kind, special.
Words with similar meanings are synonyms. Happy, joyful and cheerful are similar. Brave, bold and fearless are similar. In sad, unhappy, tearful and thrilled, thrilled is the odd one out because it is happy. In talk, discuss, kind and speak, kind is the odd one out because it is not about speaking. In noisy, quiet, silent and calm, noisy is the odd one out because the others are about peace. In cotton, wooden, silk and woollen, wooden is the odd one out because the others are fabrics.
In design the letter g is silent. In sign, high, light, night, sing and king, the g is silent in sign, light, night and high, but not in sing and king or goat, sugar and magnet. Match the qualities: kindness is being kind, bravery is being brave, wisdom is being wise, majestic is being royal, unique is being special, fierce is being strong and dedicated is being devoted.
A and an are used for one of something not named before, and the is used for a particular thing. Once upon a time, there lived a monkey on an oak tree. We use an before a vowel sound, as in an apple, an old man and an olive. We use the when we mean something specific: It gave the pear to an elephant means that particular pear. The naughty monkey snatched the bag. The dog found the apple and stole it.
Ask elders about a historical place near you. In your presentation say the name of the place and the monument, the historical people connected with it, its special features, how people feel about it and other facts. You can also make a fort puzzle: draw a fort on thick paper, cut it into pieces and put it together again.

problem.en: Fill in a, an or the: Once upon ___ time, there lived ___ monkey on ___ oak tree.

text.en: Time is the first noun, a time we do not name exactly.

why.en: Once upon a time is a fixed phrase.

text.en: Monkey starts with a consonant sound, so a monkey.
Oak starts with a vowel sound, so an oak tree.

problem.en: Which word is the odd one out: cotton, wooden, silk, woollen?

text.en: Cotton, silk and woollen are fabrics.
Wooden is made of wood.
So wooden is the odd one out.

why.en: Look for what most words have in common.

prompt.en: Tell about Maheshwar Fort and Queen Ahilya Bai in your own words.

requiredIdeas.en: A fort on a hill by the Narmada built by Queen Ahilya Bai
Red stones from Gujarat and Rajasthan
Maheshwari sarees of cotton and silk

commonMisconceptions.en: The fort was built by a king in Delhi
The fort is in Tamil Nadu

points.en: Queen Ahilya Bai of the Holkar family built Maheshwar Fort on the Narmada.
The fort has overhanging balconies and red stones from Gujarat and Rajasthan.
Maheshwari sarees are made of cotton and silk.
A and an are used for one thing, and the points to a particular thing.
Words with similar meanings help us find the odd one out.
